recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-27157; if PA wants to revise or strengthen invalid-unit behavior, that should be handled as a new tracker rather than a reconciliation edit.
issue_request: FHIR-27157 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification PA change request for R5 asking the Location near search parameter to clarify which unit string to use for miles. The final resolution says the units should be UCUM distance units, that bare mi is insufficient and [mi_us] is the miles code, and that invalid units may be reported with an OperationOutcome/HTTP 400 when the server supports near.
initial_application: The issue was applied by commits 650dd988a28c506e7f39c5086c08623f8ebfb48c, ed8eec973ee8f2eb851f30831cce8c3c66adf0d5, and d0999a3fb40cd5581118ba30af17f181f2d8ee41 in source/location/bundle-Location-search-params.xml. A later same-family FHIR-33976 commit, ecb4dd444f3c065bac2460eb9df26b4f66b2af4a, corrected the temporary 403 wording to 400 and added the algorithm caveat; fede0a93513316ea3626657108ef57a9e8f1c63a later preserved the same wording while normalizing SearchParameter formatting.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists location=Location as an active resource, so the Location search parameter bundle is in build scope. PA Confluence minutes confirm the January 2022 vote, the April 2022 decision that 403 was wrong, and the April 2022 coordination with FHIR-33976. Zulip threads show the original km/mi/[mi_us] ambiguity and a later implementer confirmation that the build text answered the question. FHIR-33976 is already represented on the combined branch by 3bba9f9bcd64aaa938e6d92cd21582eab7b7a30f.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current Location-near SearchParameter description already says servers supporting near SHALL support 'km', SHOULD support '[mi_us]', may support other units, default omitted units to kms, and MIGHT fail unrecognized units with an OperationOutcome and HTTP 400 BadRequest when near is supported.

related_jiras.note: FHIR-33976 refined the same Location-near description and sorting/algorithm guidance after FHIR-27157, corrected 403 to 400, and is already audited on the combined branch.
